videos.description:
Daft Punk and Justice meet Techno — live and unapologetically intense.
For 70 minutes, Parquet unleashes a relentless blend of driving beats, hypnotic grooves, and raw energy. Minimal gestures, maximum impact: somewhere between rock concert, warehouse rave, and avant-garde performance, the band creates a powerful live experience that pulls audiences straight onto the dancefloor. Pounding drums, haunting electronics, raw guitars, and deep basslines merge into a dark, immersive sonic journey. 
The French ensemble Parquet blends rock with electronic, noisy, and techno-inspired elements to create a distinctive sound.

videos.title: ZERALDA @ Hochschule für Musik "Hanns Eisler", Berlin | LIVE FROM BERLIN
videos.description:
“Engelein, Engelein flieg!” (Engl.: “Little Angel, Fly!”) is a song from the upcoming album ZERALDA, which moves between chanson, influences from jazz and classical music, as well as grotesque–ecstatic beats. The album is composed for voice, violin, keys, drums, and bass by musician, performer, and director Wolke Milena Wilke. Inspired by Tomi Ungerer’s fairy tale "Zeralda's Ogre" the Album explores the conflict between a longing for sensual abundance and a deep connection to all living beings, and the fear o one’s own devouring and destructive potential. The album will be released in the course of 2026.

videos.title: MAREK JOHNSON - live @ Schaubühne Lindenfels | Jazztage LEIPZIG
videos.description:
As Marek Johnson, Cologne jazz musician David Helm explores the vastness of pop. Between singer/songwriter, trip-hop, electronica and indie, they create a highly elegant sound that is both arty and accessible. Sometimes it sounds like the perfect soundtrack to long fall nights, warming you up when you start to get cold.
The quintet's music oscillates between sophistication and groundedness. The fact that the musicians have a background in jazz can be heard more in the delicate sound than in the overly atonal or intricate elements.

videos.title: CANSU TANRIKULU’S PILED UP @ JAZZEXZESS / Kantine am Berghain | LIVE FROM BERLIN
videos.description:
Theatrical absurdity, cut-up country songs, grotesque text fragments - PILED UP stages a world in which trash and depth collide, in which guilty pleasure is spotlighted from different angles. Feminist approaches to performative intimacy, absurd commercials for chastity belts, a list of sexist speeches - clichés and reality become blurred in a game full of contradictions. Musically, the project is just as radical. Pulsating synthesizers, distorted guitars and choppy rhythms drive the sound in unpredictable directions. Little pedagogy, a lot of theater, even more excess.

videos.title: ROKC MUSIC @ Peppi Guggenheim | LIVE FROM BERLIN
videos.description:
"...the four play a forward-driving music that effortlessly processes and organically combines seemingly all musical styles, including noise, dub, rock, jazz, metal, punk, and Ornette Coleman's harmolodics—either running parallel or even layered on top of each other. Naturally, such a feat can only be convincingly achieved if the musicians not only master their craft completely but also possess the ability to experiment without blinders. In the rapid shifts between shimmering single notes and tight chord playing, between control and wildness, constant progression, and bold interval leaps, the quartet demonstrates its passion for an unrelenting ride through styles and their untamed abstraction." KUHN FU is the name Berlin guitarist Christian Achim Kühn has given his multinational band, with which he has been causing a furore in the truest sense of the word on the stages of clubs and festivals since it was founded in 2012. The whole performance seems refreshingly crude and absurd, it has a lot of the anarchy of Dadaism and Surrealism, while the music is raw and mangy, shaggy and unbrushed. videos.title: BIRGITTA FLICK QUARTET @ Studio Boerne, Berlin | FILMED BY EAR
videos.description:
The Birgitta Flick Quartet is regarded as one of the most exciting projects of the young German jazz generation thanks to its remarkable musical sensitivity and virtuosic joy of playing. Since the quartet set out on its improvisatory journey nearly 15 years ago, the band has released several critically acclaimed albums, including the latest release Miniatures & Fragments (2022) and Dalarna (2016) as a septet with Lina Nyberg, Silke Eberhard and Nico Lohmann, exploring a suite that Birgitta composed inspired by traditional pastoral music and chorales from Dalarna in Sweden. 
Over the years, they have developed and refined a unique improvisatory and explorative approach to whatever notational or other musical reference they interact with, be it Birgitta’s compositions or anything they like and are inspired by — thus inspiring also Birgitta’s current artistic research investigating the entangled creative activities within the practices of composing and improvising that this video is part of. It features four new compositions created through different processes of experimenting with the topics of co-creating and notating. 

BIRGITTA FLICK QUARTET @ Studio Boerne, Berlin | 2024
FILMED BY EAR is a series by @berta.berlin.

videos.title: TRAINING with RUTH GOLLER @ Factory Studio, Berlin | FILMED BY EAR
videos.description:
TRAINING played at Moers Festival, at Jazzfest Berlin (in transatlantic cooperation with John Dieterich - from Deerhoof), at Eurojazz Mexico, Saalfelden Jazz Festival, as well as numerous club tours. Furthermore they created a concert series with a wide variety of guests in Berlin called Group TRAINING. Ruth Goller is a London-based bassist who has been involved in the development of many British experimental projects. Her musical focus has been in recent years on the development of her own project "SKYLLA", in which many of her influences get together. 
Ruth's style of composing includes microtonal bass harmonics with layers of vocal harmonies.
The three create a new, energetic music collectively: Meandering grooves, complex instrumental-vocal nestings, expressive training units, weightless unison melodies.

videos.title: Nils Wogram "Muse" - live @ Sendesaal, Bremen | FILMED BY EAR
videos.description:
Nils Wogram's music has always had a great deal of sensuality, and in this project that means all the more: All or nothing! Sound is the key component. Trombone, saxophone, harp, viola and voice are the basis for this. The visionary, Nils Wogram, who never just searches for the sake of searching, but who makes the impossible possible and the unheard of, without any compromise.
The essence is the great sensitivity with which the musicians listen to each other, how they react and interact to the sounds they create together. 
This music is lyrical and full of poetry. Some kind kind of improvised chamber music with an affinity to film, contemporary classical, folk and jazz.
Deutscher Jazzpreis/German Jazz-Award 2022 - Album Instrumental

Mit Franziska Buhre (Kuratorin Klangteppich)
Sophie Grobler, Pejman Jamilpanah, Pari (Sänger_innen)
Laura Winkler (Arrangements, Chorleitung)
Ehrengast Ali Kamrani

Moderation: Susan Zare

Laura Winkler war 2016 mit ihrer Band Holler My Dear zu Gast in Iran. 2018 entstand die Idee für einen Chor aus persischen und deutschen Muttersprachler_innen, die gemeinsam Lieder der bekannten Sängerinnen Hayedeh (1942-1990) Marzieh (1924-2010) und Ramesh (1946-2020) singen. Für den Rangarang Chor zelebriert Laura Winkler diese Sängerinnen mit neuen Arrangements einiger Lieder.

Ali Kamrani, geboren 1952 in Teheran, ist Dichter und Schauspieler. Im Alter von 20 Jahren begann er, Gedichte und Lieder zu schreiben, u.a. für die Sängerin Neli. Seit 1979 lebt Kamrani in Deutschland.

Warum bewegt uns die Popmusik Irans aus den 1960/70er noch heute? Und wie können wir die Lebenswege der Sängerinnen in Iran und im Exil heute einordnen?

Die Teilnehmenden sprechen über Teilhabe von Frauen am Musikschaffen in Iran und Ländern des globalen Nordens, Kunstfreiheit und die gemeinsame Musikpraxis über Sprach- und Geschlechtergrenzen hinweg.

Das Chorprojekt im Rahmen des Festivals Klangteppich III wird gefördert von der Bundeszentrale für politische Bildung.

Yusuf Sahilli might sound like a blues man, or a new romantic, growling about wild nights spent searching, or letting his sweet tenor voice indulge in lustful melancholy moods.
